'''Duje Dukan''' (born 4 December 1991) is a [[Croats|Croatian]] professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Klosterneuburg Dukes]] in the  [[Austrian Basketball Bundesliga]]. He played college basketball for the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]].

==Early life==
Dukan was born in [[Split, Croatia]], but moved to the United States when he was 10 months old. He grew up in [[Deerfield, Illinois]] and attended [[Deerfield High School (Illinois)|Deerfield High School]].<ref>{{cite news |author1=Rob Schultz |title=Arrives late, but worth wait |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/98166529/arrives-late-but-worth-wait/ |access-date=22 March 2022 |work=[[Wisconsin State Journal]] |date=23 February 2010 |page=B1|via =[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}}</ref> During the 1990s, Dukan was a [[ball boy]] for the [[Chicago Bulls]] at the [[United Center]].<ref>{{cite web|last1=Xypteras|first1=Tony|url=http://www.sactownroyalty.com/2015/9/2/9222675/5-things-you-didnt-know-about-duje-dukan|title=5 Things You Didn't Know About Duje Dukan|work=SactownRoyalty.com|date=2 September 2015|accessdate=4 April 2016}}</ref> He later played [[college basketball]] for the [[Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball|University of Wisconsin]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.uwbadgers.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=145|title=Duje Dukan Bio|work=UWBadgers.com|accessdate=1 July 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author1=Jim Polzin |title=Dukan even-keeled after breakthrough game |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/98166029/dukan-even-keeled-after-breakthrough-gam/ |access-date=22 March 2022 |work=[[Baraboo News Republic]] |date=13 November 2013 |page=A6|via =[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}}</ref>
<ref>{{cite news |author1=Teddy Greenstein |title=Havin' a ball, boy |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/98166272/havin-a-ball-boy/ |access-date=22 March 2022 |work=[[Chicago Tribune]] |date=14 March 2015 |page=3|via =[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Sacramento Kings (2015–2016)===
After going undrafted in the [[2015 NBA draft]], Dukan joined the [[Sacramento Kings]] for the [[2015 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web|last1=Marmolejo|first1=Erika|url=http://www.nba.com/kings/blog/get-to-know-kings-summer-league-team|title=Get To Know: Kings Summer League Team|work=NBA.com|date=1 July 2015|accessdate=1 July 2015}}</ref> On 22 July 2015, he signed with the Kings.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-acy-curry-dukan|title=Kings Sign Quincy Acy, Seth Curry and Duje Dukan|work=NBA.com|date=22 July 2015|accessdate=22 July 2015}}</ref> On 13 November 2015, he made his professional debut with the [[Reno Bighorns]] in a 123–121 loss to the [[Los Angeles D-Fenders]], scoring 14 points in 34 minutes of action as a starter.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/games/20151113/LADRNO/|title=Harris Pours in 39 as D-Fenders Win Down-to-the-Wire Season Opener Over Bighorns|work=NBA.com|date=13 November 2015|accessdate=6 January 2016}}</ref> During his rookie season, he received multiple assignments to the Bighorns, the Kings' [[NBA Development League|D-League]] affiliate.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/assignments/ |title=2015-16 NBA Assignments |work=NBA.com |accessdate=30 November 2015 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150906020056/http://dleague.nba.com/news/assignments/ |archivedate=6 September 2015 }}</ref> In the Kings' season finale on 13 April 2016, he made his long-awaited NBA debut. In 24 minutes off the bench, he recorded six points, four rebounds, one assist and one steal in a 116–81 loss to the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160413/SACHOU/gameinfo.html|title=Rockets clinch playoff berth with 116-81 win over Kings|work=NBA.com|date=13 April 2016|accessdate=13 April 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170403035221/http://www.nba.com/games/20160413/SACHOU/gameinfo.html|archive-date=3 April 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 4 July 2016, he was waived by the Kings.<ref>{{cite web|first=Nate|last=Washburn|url=http://sackings.com/Notebook/sign-of-the-times-kings-waive-butler-dukan|title=Sign of the times: Kings waive Butler, Dukan|work=SacKings.com|date=July 4, 2016|accessdate=July 4, 2016|archive-date=January 17, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170117035328/https://sackings.com/Notebook/sign-of-the-times-kings-waive-butler-dukan|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Cedevita Zagreb (2016–2017)===
On 3 August 2016, Dukan signed a three-year deal with the Croatian team [[KK Cedevita|Cedevita Zagreb]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Duje Dukan 3 godine u KK Cedeviti|url=http://www.kkcedevita.hr/vijesti/tabid/86/id/35395/duje-dukan-3-godine-u-kk-cedeviti.aspx#.V8QbF1kvk5k|website=www.kkcedevita.hr|accessdate=29 August 2016|language=hr-HR|date=3 August 2016}}</ref> Dukan left the team in January, 2017 in a mutual termination of his contract.<ref>{{cite web|title=Duje Dukan više nije igrač KK Cedevite|url=http://www.kkcedevita.hr/vijesti/tabid/86/id/35553/duje-dukan-vie-nije-igra-kk-cedevite.aspx#.WIya78s8KhA|accessdate=January 28, 2017|language=hr-HR|date=January 26, 2017}}</ref>

===Windy City Bulls (2017–2018)===
On January 27, 2017, [[Windy City Bulls]] of the [[NBA Development League]] acquired Dukan from the [[Austin Spurs]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/windy-city-bulls-acquire-duje-dukan-and-rights-of-joe-alexander-and/n-5231077|title=Windy City Bulls Acquire Duje Dukan|work=oursportscentral.com|date=January 27, 2017|accessdate=January 30, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author1=Steve Clark |title=Now healthy, former Badger Duje Dukan eyes return to NBA |url=https://eu.thenorthwestern.com/story/sports/2018/01/24/now-healthy-former-badger-duje-dukan-eyes-return-nba/1057223001/ |access-date=22 March 2022 |work=[[Oshkosh Northwestern]] |date=24 January 2018}}</ref>

===Fort Wayne Mad Ants (2018)===
On February 12, 2018, Dukan was traded by the [[Windy City Bulls]] to the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]] along with the returning player rights to [[Henry Sims]] in exchange for [[C.J. Fair]].<ref>{{cite web|website=GLeague.NBA.com|title=Mad Ants Acquire Duje Dukan and Returning Player Rights of Henry Sims|author=Stevens, Ryan|date=February 12, 2018|accessdate=February 12, 2018|url=http://fortwayne.gleague.nba.com/news/mad-ants-acquire-duje-dukan-returning-player-rights-henry-sims/}}</ref>

===2018–19 season===
On August 22, 2018, Dukan was selected by the [[Capital City Go-Go]] of the G League in the 2018 expansion draft.<ref>{{cite web|title=Capital City Go-Go Select 14 Players in 2018 NBA G League Expansion Draft|url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/capital-city-go-go-select-14-players-in-2018-nba-g-league-expansion-draft/|website=NBA.com|date=August 22, 2018|accessdate=August 22, 2018}}</ref> However, he was not added to their training camp roster.<ref>{{cite web|title=Go-Go Announce Training Camp Dates and Roster|url=https://capitalcity.gleague.nba.com/news/go-go-announce-training-camp-dates-and-roster/|website=NBA.com|date=October 21, 2018|accessdate=October 21, 2018|archive-date=October 21, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181021232741/https://capitalcity.gleague.nba.com/news/go-go-announce-training-camp-dates-and-roster/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Instead, he was added to the [[Westchester Knicks]] training camp roster<ref>{{cite web |title=Westchester Knicks Announce 2018-19 Training Camp Roster |url=https://westchester.gleague.nba.com/news/westchester-knicks-announce-2018-19-training-camp-roster/ |website=NBA.com |accessdate=October 23, 2018 |date=October 23, 2018 |archive-date=July 20, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190720013334/https://westchester.gleague.nba.com/news/westchester-knicks-announce-2018-19-training-camp-roster/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> but did not make the final roster. Dukan ultimately landed with the [[Oklahoma City Blue]] in November, but was waived after three games. He signed with the [[Capital City Go-Go]] in January 2019.

===2019–20 season===
On July 19, 2019, Dukan signed a one-year deal with Spanish club [[CB Estudiantes|Movistar Estudiantes]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Duje Dukan signs with Estudiantes |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/duje-dukan-signs-with-estudiantes/ |accessdate=19 July 2019 |work=Sportando |date=19 July 2019 |archive-date=19 July 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190719123356/https://sportando.basketball/en/duje-dukan-signs-with-estudiantes/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> He averaged 4.7 points and 1.8 rebounds per game in ACB play.<ref name="tau">{{cite web |title=Duje Dukan joins Tau Castellon |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/duje-dukan-joins-tau-castellon/ |website=Sportando |accessdate=August 8, 2020 |date=August 8, 2020}}</ref>

===2020–21 season===
On August 8, 2020, Dukan signed with [[AB Castelló|TAU Castelló]] of the [[Liga Española de Baloncesto|LEB Oro]].<ref name="tau" /> He averaged 6.9 points and 2.4 rebounds per game.<ref name="Caceres" />

===2021–22 season===
On October 5, 2021, Dukan signed with [[Cáceres Ciudad del Baloncesto]] of the Spanish [[LEB Oro]].<ref name="Caceres">{{cite web |title=Caceres land Duje Dukan |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Croatia/news/707461/Caceres-land-Duje-Dukan |website=Eurobasket |access-date=October 5, 2021 |date=October 5, 2021}}</ref>

=== 2022–23 season ===
On November 23, 2022, Dukan joined Dutch team [[Landstede Hammers]] of the [[BNXT League]], where he replaced [[Ryan Davis (basketball)|Ryan Davis]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-11-23 |title=Dukan replaces Davis at Landstede |url=https://bnxtleague.com/en/newsvideo/dukan-replaces-davis-at-landstede |access-date=2022-11-24 |website=bnxtleague.com}}</ref>

==Personal life==
His father, [[Ivica Dukan]], played basketball professionally in Europe for 15 years and is now an international basketball scout for the Chicago Bulls.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Dauster|first1=Rob|url=http://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2015/03/13/wisconsins-duje-dukan-went-from-united-center-ballboy-to-a-starring-role/|title=Wisconsin's Duje Dukan went from United Center ballboy to a starring role|work=NBCSports.com|date=13 March 2015|accessdate=13 March 2015}}</ref>
